names: Propane-1,2-diol esters of fatty acids, propylene glycol esters of fatty acids

more_info.overview: Propylene glycol esters of fatty acids are mixtures of mono- and diesters combining propane-1,2-diol with edible fatty acids. Its emulsifying role is to help form or maintain mixtures of oil and water in the finished food. A mixture of propylene glycol esters of fatty acids found in edible fats and oils. The fatty-acid feedstock is not restricted to a single biological source. The specified material is supplied as white flakes or liquid.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; sweet baked goods; frozen desserts.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.daily_intake: 25 mg propylene glycol/kg body weight/day, equivalent to 80 mg E477/kg body weight/day under the specified composition limit (EFSA, 2018).
more_info.origin: A mixture of propylene glycol esters of fatty acids found in edible fats and oils. The fatty-acid feedstock is not restricted to a single biological source.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The fatty-acid feedstock is not specified as exclusively plant derived. Vegan, vegetarian, halal and kosher suitability cannot be established without the supplier identifying the raw material and processing.
more_info.side_effects:
Refined food-use estimates remained below the limit.
EFSA requested consideration of combined propylene-glycol exposure from related authorised ingredients.
